set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, on the road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs into the canyon and breaks down across boulder fields, so pick it up again on the far side and stay on the north side of the creek. At the Meadows camping zone the trail divides: the south fork heads for the saddle between Middle and South Teton, and the way to the Lower Saddle stays on the creek's north side. Take the south fork toward the Ellingwood Couloir; the route starts just to the right of that couloir.

review.notes: Start location from the route page; south fork access to the Ellingwood Couloir from the Buckingham and Ellingwood pages; Meadows junction from the Garnet Canyon timings page. Descent skipped: no source says where the ridge ends beyond 'leads to the Dike Pinnacle'.

set.approach: Follow the Garnet Canyon trail from the Lupine Meadows trailhead to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft. From the saddle, head southwest to the two pinnacles at the foot of Middle Teton's north ridge. Pass the lower one, Pinocchio Pinnacle, on its west side, then cross the notch between the two; Bonney's Pinnacle is the higher one on the right, and the scramble starts from that notch.

review.notes: Pinnacle layout from three route pages; Lower Saddle distance as in the reviewed Grand Teton batch. Descent skipped: no source says how to get off.

set.descent_text: The ridge ends on the south summit, which is awkward to leave: a short rappel drops into the notch toward the main summit, and a walk from there reaches the highest point. From the top, go down the Southwest Couloir, a class 3 route that finishes at the saddle between Middle and South Teton, then descend the south fork of Garnet Canyon to the Meadows and the Garnet Canyon trail. Expect firm snow in the Ellingwood Couloir early in the season, so carry an ice axe.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, on the road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs into the canyon and breaks down across boulder fields, so pick it up again on the far side and stay on the north side of the creek. At the Meadows camping zone the trail divides: the south fork heads for the saddle between Middle and South Teton, and the way to the Lower Saddle stays on the creek's north side. Go up the south fork to the Ellingwood Couloir, which usually holds moderately steep snow; the ridge is the broad buttress forming its left side, and most parties reach it by climbing the couloir, so boots that suit firm snow and an ice axe are needed.

review.notes: Descent from the route page and the south-chimney page, SW couloir as the easiest way down from the Ellingwood page; approach from the route and variation pages.

set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, on the road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs into the canyon and breaks down across boulder fields, so pick it up again on the far side and stay on the north side of the creek. At the Meadows camping zone the trail divides: the south fork heads for the saddle between Middle and South Teton, and the way to the Lower Saddle stays on the creek's north side. Take the south fork to the ridge immediately west of the Buckingham Ridge. The ridge is reached from the couloirs on either side of it; they hold snow for much of the season, and once melted out they become loose and hazardous.

review.notes: Ridge position and access couloirs from the route page and Buckingham page. Descent skipped: no source says where it tops out.

set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit of the Dike Pinnacle. From there you can descend the pinnacle's east side back to the lower Middle Teton Glacier, then work down the glacier and out toward Garnet Canyon. The other choice is to continue by the Dike Route toward Middle Teton, which means a rappel to Ellingwood Col, a steep snow crossing and the east face; that line then returns by the Southwest Couloir. Carry an ice axe for the glacier.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, on the road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs into the canyon and breaks down across boulder fields, so pick it up again on the far side and stay on the north side of the creek. At the Meadows camping zone the trail divides: the south fork heads for the saddle between Middle and South Teton, and the way to the Lower Saddle stays on the creek's north side. The Middle Teton Glacier lies below the peak's north side, along the way to the Lower Saddle. The route starts about halfway up the glacier, so cross the lower ice to its base; an ice axe is essential and crampons may be needed.

review.notes: Route page gives the two ways off the pinnacle; Dike Route page confirms a bail onto the glacier and the Ellingwood Col crossing; glacier location from the Glacier Route page.

set.descent_text: The final descent from the summit is the Southwest Couloir, a class 3 scramble to the saddle between Middle and South Teton, then down the south fork of Garnet Canyon to the Meadows. Many parties do not go on to the summit at all: after the Dike Pinnacle they bail out by dropping into Garnet Canyon's south fork, or by heading north onto the Middle Teton Glacier. The ground from the pinnacle to Ellingwood Col is convoluted and needs a rappel, and the col itself is a steep snow crossing of about 40 degrees that holds snow all year.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, on the road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs into the canyon and breaks down across boulder fields, so pick it up again on the far side and stay on the north side of the creek. At the Meadows camping zone the trail divides: the south fork heads for the saddle between Middle and South Teton, and the way to the Lower Saddle stays on the creek's north side. The route follows the obvious black dike on the east face of the Dike Pinnacle, the eastern sub-peak of Middle Teton, which can be studied from the meadows. Snow on the dike and the face can be scouted from there before committing.

review.notes: Route page for the whole climb and its bail options; SW couloir descent agreed by the Southwest Couloir and Glacier pages. Approach to the base is only described as the dike on the east face, so kept general.

set.descent_text: The easiest way down is the Southwest Couloir, which is class 3 and finishes at the saddle between Middle and South Teton. From the saddle, drop into the south fork of Garnet Canyon, follow it to the Meadows, and take the Garnet Canyon trail out. Carry an ice axe while snow remains; once the snow is gone the Ellingwood Couloir is wet, loose and prone to rockfall.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, on the road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs into the canyon and breaks down across boulder fields, so pick it up again on the far side and stay on the north side of the creek. At the Meadows camping zone the trail divides: the south fork heads for the saddle between Middle and South Teton, and the way to the Lower Saddle stays on the creek's north side. Take the south fork of the canyon to the south side of the peak. From the trailhead to the summit the day involves about 6,000 ft of gain, of which roughly 2,000 ft is climbing. The couloir holds snow up to about 45 degrees; it joins the Middle Teton Glacier route higher up.

review.notes: Couloir description, 6,000 ft gain and SW couloir descent from the route page; gain and south fork from the Next Summit guide.

set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, on the road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs into the canyon and breaks down across boulder fields, so pick it up again on the far side and stay on the north side of the creek. At the Meadows camping zone the trail divides: the south fork heads for the saddle between Middle and South Teton, and the way to the Lower Saddle stays on the creek's north side. The Middle Teton Glacier is the obvious snow-and-ice line seen on the way toward the Lower Saddle, on the peak's north side. The left side of the upper tongue avoids a large crevasse that opens in mid to late season. The route changes from year to year, so ice axe and crampons are normal equipment.

review.notes: Glacier position and crevasse from the route page; glacier location also from the Dike Pinnacle and North Wall pages.

set.descent_text: Two ways down are in regular use. The more usual one is to downclimb the Southwest Couloir, a class 3 route to the saddle between Middle and South Teton, and descend the south fork of Garnet Canyon. The other is to traverse north back across the east side of the summit block to a gap leading west above the black dike notch, rappel into that notch, and retrace the ridge to the Lower Saddle and the Garnet Canyon trail.
set.approach: Follow the Garnet Canyon trail from the Lupine Meadows trailhead to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft. From the saddle, go southwest to the two pinnacles at the foot of the ridge. Pass the first, Pinocchio Pinnacle, on its west side and the higher one, Bonney's Pinnacle, on its east side. Beyond Bonney's a notch left by a small dike marks the start of the ridge route proper.

review.notes: Approach and the rappel/retrace descent from the North Ridge page; SW couloir from the NW Ice Couloir page; retrace of the north ridge also in the existing Glacier Route row text.

set.descent_text: The route finishes just below the summit of Middle Teton. Go down the Southwest Couloir, a class 3 route to the saddle between Middle and South Teton, then take the south fork of Garnet Canyon to the Meadows and the trail out. Snow can remain in the couloir early in the season, so keep an axe handy.
set.approach: Follow the Garnet Canyon trail from the Lupine Meadows trailhead to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft. From the saddle, head up toward the north ridge. Pass the lower pinnacle, Pinocchio Pinnacle, on its west side and the higher one, Bonney's Pinnacle, on its east side to reach a notch below the main wall. Climb out of the notch and traverse right on loose ledges to the start of the ice and snow couloir.

review.notes: Approach agreed by the route and North Ridge pages; descent from the route page and the SW couloir page.

set.approach: Follow the Garnet Canyon trail from the Lupine Meadows trailhead to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft. Pinocchio Pinnacle is the lower of the two pinnacles at the foot of Middle Teton's north ridge. From the saddle, go around its west side to the gap separating it from Bonney's Pinnacle, where the face begins.

review.notes: Pinnacle layout from three pages. Descent skipped: no source describes it.

set.descent_text: The variation ends on the south summit. A rappel from there reaches the notch toward the main summit, and a short walk gains the highest point. Descend by the Southwest Couloir, the usual way down, to the saddle between Middle and South Teton, then work down Garnet Canyon's south fork as far as the Meadows. Snow may linger on the lower ridge and on the descent, so an ice axe is advisable.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, on the road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs into the canyon and breaks down across boulder fields, so pick it up again on the far side and stay on the north side of the creek. At the Meadows camping zone the trail divides: the south fork heads for the saddle between Middle and South Teton, and the way to the Lower Saddle stays on the creek's north side. Go up the south fork to the Ellingwood Couloir, whose moderately steep snow is the usual access to the Buckingham buttress on its left side. The chimney lies high on that ridge, directly below the south summit, and can be seen from the south fork when the light is right; it is entered from a ledge near the top of the standard route's seventh pitch.

review.notes: Variation page for the finish and descent; standard ridge approach from the Buckingham page. The base of this variation is partway up the ridge, not the bottom.

set.descent_text: This couloir is the usual way down for the whole peak, so a party simply retraces the ascent to the saddle between Middle and South Teton. Go all the way past the saddle before turning east, because the snowfield northeast of it is steep early in the season. The couloir is narrow near its top and acts as a bowling alley with anyone above, so helmets matter. Expect snow in early season and talus with some scrambling later, then follow the south fork of Garnet Canyon down to the Meadows and the trail.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, on the road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs into the canyon and breaks down across boulder fields, so pick it up again on the far side and stay on the north side of the creek. At the Meadows camping zone the trail divides: the south fork heads for the saddle between Middle and South Teton, and the way to the Lower Saddle stays on the creek's north side. Climb the south fork all the way to the saddle between Middle and South Teton; do not branch off to the right early. From there the couloir is plainly visible to the west of the summit ridge. About 6,000 ft of gain separates the trailhead from the top, and the way up the canyon is mostly route-finding by cairns and trail fragments.

review.notes: Route page, Next Summit guide and Ellingwood page agree on the south fork, the saddle and the 6,000 ft total gain.

wy_middle_finger_northwall_taylor_inge_s.skip_reason: Row combines several unfinished north wall lines (only Taylor is said to reach the summit); one source, and it gives no descent. Not safe to attach a descent or approach.
